name: FormWizard
summary: A long form split into steps: a Stepper, one panel per step, back and next, a review step and a submit at the end. Each step is checked before the user moves past it.
useWhen: A form with more than about eight fields that falls into three to seven groups with an order: checkout, onboarding, an application
Later steps depend on answers in earlier ones, so the user should finish them in order
The user should check every answer on a review step before sending
avoidWhen: A short form that fits on one screen
Settings the user changes one at a time, in any order
Steps that are separate tasks and save on their own

insteadUse.Settings in any order: Tabs with a Form per tab

steps.description: One entry per step: id, title (a short noun), description, content (a node, or a function of { values, errors } to show errors and the review), validate (values to errors by field name, may be async), nextLabel, backLabel.

mode.description: Passed to the Stepper. linear: a later step opens only when the ones before it passed their check. free: any step; moving forward still checks the current step, and submit checks every step. Read once, at mount, with the number of steps.

onSubmit.description: Called with every value of every step when the last step is sent. While a promise runs the state is submitting and the submit button shows the sending status. When it resolves the state is done. When it rejects the wizard goes back to editing, shows the submitError words in the error part and says them once.

submitLabel.description: The submit button on the last step: a verb plus a noun, Place order. Arabic default إرسال النموذج.

done.description: Shown in the panel after a successful submit.

doneTitle.description: The heading after a successful submit, also said by the status.

orientation.description: The Stepper layout, on the Stepper's data-orientation. Vertical puts the steps in a column at the start side; on a phone they stack above the panel.

size.description: The Stepper size, the action buttons and the title size.

stepsLabel.description: The name of the steps list: Checkout steps.

labels.description: Default words: next, back, submit, required, done, submitError, checking, sending, separator. English Go to next step, Go to previous step, Send form, Fill in this field, Form sent. Arabic الانتقال للخطوة التالية، الرجوع للخطوة السابقة، إرسال النموذج، هذا الحقل مطلوب، تم الإرسال. Demos pass a verb plus a noun per step instead.

defaultErrors.description: Errors by step index, then field name, shown before the user checks a step: errors a server sent back. A step's own check replaces its entry.

formProps.description: Props of the panel form: name, action, autoComplete.

a11y.role: The panel is a form named by the step title (aria-labelledby). The steps are a Stepper list. The status is a polite live region.
a11y.focus: Tab order: the steps the user may reach, then the fields of the current step, then back and next. On a step change focus moves to the step title (tabindex -1), which shows the focus ring. A failed check moves focus to the first field with an error, after the error is linked to it.

keys.Tab: Moves through the steps, the fields and the actions, in that order
keys.Enter: In a single line field: checks the step and moves to the next one, or sends the form on the last step. On a step: goes to that step

a11y.announce: On a step change the status says the position and the title once: Step 2 of 4, Address (WCAG 4.1.3). After a submit it says the done title. Field errors are read with their field through aria-describedby when focus lands there.
notes: Every step stays in the DOM; steps that are not current carry hidden. What the user typed is kept when they go back, and is never asked for twice (WCAG 3.3.7). autocomplete values on the fields are kept as given.

The panel is noValidate. The wizard checks one step at a time: an empty field marked required on its Field gets the required words, then the browser's constraint validation (type, pattern, min, max), then the step's validate function.
The next button is the form's submit button, so Enter in a field moves on. Back is type button.
One check or submit runs at a time: a second Enter while a check runs does nothing, and Back and the steps are inactive until it ends. A check that resolves after the user moved away is dropped.
Form (1.4.1) will render the panel later, as <Form data-part="panel">, and bring the error summary and the server error mapping. Until then the panel is a plain form and works with Field.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip.

en.title: Each step a short noun: Account, Address, Delivery, Review.
en.buttons: A verb plus a noun that names what happens: Save address, Review order, Place order, Edit account. Never Next, Back, Continue or OK on their own.
en.errors: Say what is wrong and how to fix it: Enter the five digit postal code.
en.review: The last step shows every answer with its label, so the user can check before sending.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: الحساب، العنوان، التوصيل، المراجعة.
ar.buttons: Noun form labels: حفظ العنوان، مراجعة الطلب، إرسال الطلب، تعديل الحساب.
ar.errors: White Saudi dialect, direct: اكتب الرمز البريدي من خمسة أرقام.
ar.digits: Western digits in the status: الخطوة 2 من 4.

react.behavior: hand built on a native form; Stepper; state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts
react.note: Motion fade-rise: the current step body fades in and rises by space.xs through @starting-style; under reduced motion it only fades, and every duration is 0ms.

angular.behavior: [dsFormWizard] on a div with a form panel in its template and the dsStepper, state from packages/shared/src/stepper.ts
angular.note: A step content is a TemplateRef with values and errors in its context. onSubmit is a function input, onStepChange the stepChange output, formProps a record of attributes for the panel form, formRef the formElement of exportAs dsFormWizard. FormWizard.css and Stepper.css are used as is.

native.behavior: react-native:View with a Stepper, one step mounted with its values held in state
native.note: On phones the Stepper is vertical or a compact Step 2 of 4 line; the keyboard avoids the actions.

styles.studio: Flat: the panel sits on the surface, a hairline above the actions, the next button the neutral fill.
styles.desk: The next and submit buttons are the yellow primary; the Stepper takes the yellow family.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.right: A verb plus a noun per step: Save address, Edit account

mistakes.wrong: Steps unmounted on next, so going back shows empty fields
mistakes.right: FormWizard, which keeps every step in the form and hides the ones that are not current

mistakes.wrong: A wizard for a form of four fields
Checking every field only at the end
mistakes.right: A validate function per step, so errors show where the user is

mistakes.wrong: Sending the form with no review step
mistakes.right: A last step whose content shows every value with its label
